title: Baked Mac and Cheese
seoTitle: Baked Mac and Cheese | Firefighter Meal
subtitle: Creamy, bubbling, hall-approved mac
description: Creamy, bubbling, hall-approved mac. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Hotel pans or large baking dishes

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Baked Mac and Cheese in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use Sharp cheddar, shredded as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch vegetarian. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Par-cook the macaroni
steps.instruction: Boil elbow macaroni in well-salted water 2 minutes shy of al dente — it finishes in the oven. Drain thoroughly; wet pasta makes a soupy bake.

steps.title: Make the cheese sauce
steps.instruction: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat. Whisk in flour; cook 1 minute. Whisk in milk in steady streams until smooth. Simmer until thick enough to coat a spoon, then melt in cheddar and gruyere off the heat. Stir in Dijon, salt, and pepper.

steps.title: Combine pasta and sauce
steps.instruction: Fold drained macaroni into cheese sauce until every piece is coated. The sauce should look slightly loose — pasta absorbs liquid in the oven.

steps.title: Pan up and add topping
steps.instruction: Transfer to buttered hotel pans. Mix panko with melted butter and parmesan; scatter evenly over the top for a crunchy lid. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Bake until bubbling
steps.instruction: Bake at 375°F 25–30 minutes until edges bubble and topping is deep golden. If the top browns before the center is hot, cover with foil and continue baking.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F for any egg-based components. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.instruction: Rest 5 minutes so the bake sets — scoops hold together on the line. Serve with a spatula, not a spoon, for clean portions. Bake until the center reaches a safe internal temp (165°F for any egg-based components) and edges look set — use a thermometer at the thickest point. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Scoop baked mac from hotel pans with a spatula so the breadcrumb lid stays intact.
Keep backup pan warming at 200°F — mac tightens as it holds; splash milk when reheating.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Creamy, bubbling, hall-approved mac. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — Baked Mac and Cheese runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
